name: Lattice Gas Automaton
miniText: NetLogo Lattice Gas Automaton investigates how reversible local collision rules produce propagating density patterns. Binary occupied cells undergo alternating even and odd two-by-two block updates; reversing the order retraces the original evolution on an even-sized periodic grid. Develops transport properties of the classical lattice-gas family cited in the model Info [1]. Introduces improved lattice symmetry for the Navier-Stokes setting, a key contrast with square-grid rules [2]. Provides the statistical-mechanical interpretation of cellular automaton dynamics [3]. The NetLogo source calls this HPP-like construction limited; square-grid symmetry and discrete velocities prevent assuming general isotropic hydrodynamic validity from circular-looking waves. The simulation illustrates reversibility, conserved local motion and the importance of lattice geometry. Reproducing these patterns establishes rule fidelity, not empirical validation.
